title: Google opens a shared Connected Apps integration path for Gemini and Search
dek: A developer can register one authorized tool integration for both surfaces using a remote MCP server or Android AppFunctions.
evidence: Google platform announcement and developer documentation; preview access and no independent reliability data
takeaway: Design connector actions as authenticated, scoped APIs with idempotency and confirmation; a shared discovery surface is not shared authorization.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: An app previously needed separate product-specific integration work to expose user data and actions to different assistant surfaces.

paragraphs: Connector fragmentation: An app previously needed separate product-specific integration work to expose user data and actions to different assistant surfaces.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Google's preview supports a cloud-hosted Model Context Protocol server or Android MCP through AppFunctions. Remote MCP exposes server tools; AppFunctions can invoke supported native Android app functions on-device.
Google Connected Console handles tool registration, testing, review and publication. Developers choose Search, Gemini or both, and can inspect traffic, latency and error rates after launch.
Google's developer guide describes OAuth 2.1 for remote MCP authorization. Users link an account; the tool server still must enforce each user's access rights and action scope.

paragraphs: Two integration paths: Google's preview supports a cloud-hosted Model Context Protocol server or Android MCP through AppFunctions. Remote MCP exposes server tools; AppFunctions can invoke supported native Android app functions on-device.

One registration flow: Google Connected Console handles tool registration, testing, review and publication. Developers choose Search, Gemini or both, and can inspect traffic, latency and error rates after launch.
User authorization: Google's developer guide describes OAuth 2.1 for remote MCP authorization. Users link an account; the tool server still must enforce each user's access rights and action scope.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: Google says more than 50 Connected Apps already exist across Search and Gemini, while the unified developer platform itself is preview-only with phased access.
Google did not publish cross-surface success rates, end-to-end latency distributions, OAuth failure rates or an independent security assessment for the new integration path.
Build once does not mean identical permissions or behavior on every surface. Product review, user consent, tool availability and local versus remote execution can differ.

paragraphs: Current footprint: Google says more than 50 Connected Apps already exist across Search and Gemini, while the unified developer platform itself is preview-only with phased access.
Missing measurements: Google did not publish cross-surface success rates, end-to-end latency distributions, OAuth failure rates or an independent security assessment for the new integration path.
Scope of reuse: Build once does not mean identical permissions or behavior on every surface. Product review, user consent, tool availability and local versus remote execution can differ.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Validate user identity and tenant scope at execution, not only when a model selects a tool. Use explicit confirmation for purchases, messages and other irreversible writes.
Test duplicate invocations, partial failures, expired grants and cancellation across both Search and Gemini. A repeated model action should not repeat a payment or destructive update.

paragraphs: Treat tools as public APIs: Validate user identity and tenant scope at execution, not only when a model selects a tool. Use explicit confirmation for purchases, messages and other irreversible writes.

Make retries safe: Test duplicate invocations, partial failures, expired grants and cancellation across both Search and Gemini. A repeated model action should not repeat a payment or destructive update.
